title: Time machine and favorite bands; Fats Navarro
summary: He would love to hear Parker, Armstrong, Lester Young, Ellington and Blakey; favorites include Bird and Fats and Fats Navarro.

bands.name: Charlie Parker and Fats Navarro band

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: If you could go in a time machine and go back to some musical moments in the history of jazz, do you have anything that you’d like to be?

Oh well I would have loved to see Charlie Parker. I would have loved to see Louis Armstrong in the 20’s, late 20’s, ’27, ’28. I would have loved to see Lester Young with the Basie Band in the 40’s, and Sweets Edison. I would have loved to hear Duke Ellington like in the 60’s. And I should say I would have loved to hear Louis Armstrong anytime [inaudible]. I would have loved to hear like Art Blakey’s bands in the 60’s. All that.
I hear some Art Blakey in your music. I mean I hear that kind of that unbridled energy in some of the tunes and stuff, remember that Blue Note —

I love that period. I love the 50’s, I love the 60’s too. I love the Freddie Hubbard band and the Lee Morgan band. But yeah, I [inaudible]. I love Bird too. Bird and Fats was probably my favorite band if I had to pick one, it would be with Bird with Fats, “One Night at Birdland” with Bud Powell and Tommy Potter and I guess Art Blakey is on the record. Roy Haynes sits in on the record. That’s one of my favorites of all time. I love Fats Navarro. He is one of my first influences. But after that period of Clifford, like at college, it was 1982, at the end of ’82 and ’83, that was where I missed out. I had got a Fats Navarro with the thing he did with Howard McGhee. And I copied all of his solos. You know, what I could play. Some of the stuff I couldn’t play. But the stuff that I could handle technically I played it every day with the tape.
